title: U.S. House · Ohio's 15th District
area: Central Ohio, including Fairfield, Pickaway and part of Franklin counties.

context.text: Incumbent Mike Carey (R) advanced from the May 5, 2026 Republican primary; Samuel Ronan appeared on that primary's ballot but was disqualified, and he is now running in the general election as an independent write-in candidate. Don Leonard (D) defeated Adam Miller in the Democratic primary. Brennan Barrington won the Libertarian primary. Gary Josephson is also running as an independent write-in candidate.

summary.text: Mike Carey is the Republican incumbent seeking re-election in Ohio's 15th Congressional District, which he has represented since winning a November 2021 special election. Before Congress he spent more than 20 years as an energy-industry executive, including as president of the Ohio Coal Association. He serves on the House Ways and Means Committee and the Committee on House Administration.

background.text: Born in 1971 and raised in Sabina, Ohio, where, according to his official biography, he grew up on the family farm; graduated from East Clinton High School (1989).
Earned an A.S. in economics from Marion Military Institute (1991) and a B.A. in history from Ohio State University (1993).
Served in the U.S. Army Reserve from 1989 to 1999; his official biography says he attended Marion Military Institute on an ROTC scholarship and served as an officer.

Worked for more than 20 years as an energy-industry executive, including as vice president of government affairs at American Consolidated Natural Resources and at Murray Energy Corporation, and as chairman of the board and president of the Ohio Coal Association.
Won the November 2, 2021 special general election for Ohio's 15th District with 58.3% of the vote over Democrat Allison Russo, succeeding Steve Stivers; he was sworn in on November 4, 2021.
Won re-election on November 8, 2022 (57.0%, over Gary Josephson) and November 5, 2024 (56.5%, over Adam Miller), and advanced unopposed from the May 5, 2026 Republican primary.
His official page lists his committee assignments as House Ways and Means (Subcommittees on Work and Welfare and on Social Security) and House Administration (Subcommittee on Modernization).
According to his official biography, he lives in Columbus with his wife, Meghan, and is a father of three and a grandfather.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Ways and Means (Social Security and Work and Welfare subcommittees), the House Committee on Budget, and the Committee on House Administration's Modernization and Innovation Subcommittee (119th Congress, 2025-2026).

summary.text: Don Leonard is the Democratic nominee for Ohio's 15th Congressional District. He is a professor of city and regional planning at The Ohio State University and a former U.S. Peace Corps volunteer, and he won the May 5, 2026 Democratic primary over Adam Miller. In his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey he describes his campaign as centered on household costs for working families.

background.text: In his Ballotpedia survey, describes growing up as the son of a single mother and says his childhood included periods when poverty and homelessness were close.
Earned a bachelor's degree in political science (2001) and a master's degree in regional development (2003) from the University of Massachusetts, Lowell.
Served two years in the U.S. Peace Corps in South America after college, according to his survey.
Earned a Ph.D. in government from Cornell University (2013).
Works as a professor of city and regional planning at The Ohio State University.
Defeated Adam Miller in the May 5, 2026 Democratic primary, 52.9% to 47.1%.
Says he and his wife had a daughter in January 2025 and that the birth was part of his decision to run for office.

summary.text: Brennan Barrington is the Libertarian Party nominee for Ohio's 15th Congressional District. He holds an aerospace engineering degree from Ohio State University and is a member of the Libertarian Party of Ohio's Central Committee. In his survey he lists cutting taxes, spending and regulations and changing how elections are conducted among his campaign messages.

background.text: Says he was born and raised in central Ohio and has lived there for all but two years of his life.
Graduated from Licking Heights High School and earned a Bachelor of Science in aerospace engineering from Ohio State University in 2019.
Describes himself as an advocate for electoral reform since the 2016 elections.

Has twice been a delegate to the Libertarian National Convention, once serving on its Platform Committee, and is a member of the Libertarian Party of Ohio's Central Committee, according to his survey.
Advanced unopposed from the May 5, 2026 Libertarian primary, receiving 489 votes.

candidates.name: Gary Josephson
candidates.ballotNote: Filed as an independent write-in candidate.

summary.text: Gary Josephson is an independent write-in candidate for Ohio's 15th Congressional District. He was the Democratic nominee for the seat in 2022, losing to Mike Carey, and describes a long background as a union leader and community organizer.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree from Ohio State University in 1980.

In a 2022 Ballotpedia survey, described himself as an activist for more than 50 years, with experience as a union representative, community activist and youth worker, and as president of CWA Local 4501.
Said he studied elections, legislation, environment, constitution, banking, arbitration and international human rights at the Ohio State University law school.
Finished fifth with 6.6% in the April 28, 2020 Democratic primary for Ohio House District 25.
Won the May 3, 2022 Democratic primary for Ohio's 15th District unopposed, then lost the November 8, 2022 general election to Mike Carey, 43.0% to 57.0%.

candidates.name: Samuel Ronan
candidates.ballotNote: Ran in and was disqualified from the Republican primary; running in the general election as an independent write-in candidate.

summary.text: Samuel Ronan is an independent write-in candidate for Ohio's 15th Congressional District. A U.S. Air Force veteran who works in manufacturing, he ran in the 2026 Republican primary but was disqualified, and previously ran for office as a Democrat. He describes his campaign as focused on the cost of living and accountability for powerful institutions.

background.text: According to his Ballotpedia survey, grew up in Lancaster, Ohio, graduated from Lancaster High School in 2008, and lives in Grove City.
Served in the U.S. Air Force beginning in 2009, reaching the rank of staff sergeant according to his survey, and earned an associate degree from the Community College of the Air Force in 2011.
Career experience includes maintenance technician and metrology roles at manufacturing companies, including VSP One Columbus, Abbott Nutrition and Keysight.

Ran as the Democratic nominee for Ohio House District 62 in 2016, losing to Republican Scott Lipps, 78.6% to 21.4%; separately, his filing for the 2016 U.S. House race in Ohio's 1st District was not certified by the Hamilton County Board of Elections.
Was a candidate for chair of the Democratic National Committee in 2017, according to Ballotpedia.
Appeared on the May 5, 2026 Republican primary ballot but was disqualified; he is now a write-in independent.

sources.title: United States House of Representatives elections in Ohio, 2026

researchNotes: Ballotpedia profiles for write-in candidates Gary Josephson and Samuel Ronan contain limited biographical detail; Josephson's is drawn largely from a 2022 survey and Ronan's sources give differing Air Force service end years, so none is stated. Barrington's Ballotpedia profile contains no statement of issues. Neither Carey nor Leonard's campaign website was available for review, so their priorities and positions are omitted rather than inferred. Federal key votes and FEC finance totals for Carey are added separately.
